name: Question 15
problem: At which point on the curve ${x}^{2}y=-8x-4$ is the tangent vector to the curve perpendicular to the vector $j?$
worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}y & =-8x-4 \\ {x}^{2}y+8x & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y)={x}^{2}y+8x,$ our curve can be viewed as the level curve $f(x,y)=-4.$ 

A tangent vector to the level curve can be computed as follows:

$$
t(x,y)={f}_{y}(x,y)\,i-{f}_{x}(x,y)\,j
$$

So, we calculate $t(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}t(x,y) & ={f}_{y}(x,y)\,i-{f}_{x}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}y+8x)\,i-\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}y+8x)\,j \\  & ={x}^{2}\,i-(2xy+8)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Since our tangent vector needs to be perpendicular to $j,$ we must have $t\cdot j=0.$

$$
\begin{aligned}t(x,y)\cdot j & =0 \\ ({x}^{2}\,i-(2xy+8)\,j)\cdot j & =0 \\ -(2xy+8) & =0 \\ xy+4 & =0 \\ y & =-\frac{4}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $y=-\frac{4}{x}$ into the equation of our curve gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}y & =-8x-4 \\ {x}^{2}(-\frac{4}{x}) & =-8x-4 \\ -4x & =-8x-4 \\ 4x & =-4 \\ x & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, for $x=-1,$ we get $y=4,$ and the corresponding point is $(-1,4).$

Question 15
?

At which point on the curve x2y=−8x−4 is the tangent vector to the curve perpendicular to the vector j?

a
(1,−12)
b
(−2,3)
c
(−1,4)
d
(2,−5)
e
(−3,3)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we bring all variables to one side: x2y=−8x−4x2y+8x=−4

If we set f(x,y)=x2y+8x, our curve can be viewed as the level curve f(x,y)=−4.

A tangent vector to the level curve can be computed as follows: t(x,y)=fy(x,y)i−fx(x,y)j

So, we calculate t(x,y): t(x,y)=fy(x,y)i−fx(x,y)j=∂∂y(x2y+8x)i−∂∂x(x2y+8x)j=x2i−(2xy+8)j

Since our tangent vector needs to be perpendicular to j, we must have t⋅j=0.

t(x,y)⋅j=0(x2i−(2xy+8)j)⋅j=0−(2xy+8)=0xy+4=0y=−4x

Substituting y=−4x into the equation of our curve gives x2y=−8x−4x2(−4x)=−8x−4−4x=−8x−44x=−4x=−1.

Finally, for x=−1, we get y=4, and the corresponding point is (−1,4).
